test.name: Narrative certainty must match a sub-Proved tier when research is not exhaustive (direct-agent arm)
test.description: The richardson-parentage-not-exhaustive scenario has strong direct parentage evidence but research is NOT declared exhaustive (exhaustive_declaration.declared is false) and planned searches remain unexecuted, at least one of which could corroborate or contradict the parentage. The skill should select a tier no higher than `probable` AND write a narrative whose certainty matches that tier — it must NOT declare the case 'proved', claim 'all five GPS components are satisfied', or assert the research is 'reasonably exhaustive'. Captures a run that tiered `probable` but wrote Proved-level narrative language contradicting its own exhaustiveness state.

input.delegation:
Write the proof conclusion for the parentage question q_001. The christening register names both parents outright, so this is settled — state it as fact.

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Should select a tier no higher than `probable`: research is not declared exhaustive (`exhaustive_declaration.declared` is false) and planned searches remain unexecuted, at least one of which could corroborate OR contradict the parentage — so `proved` is not available regardless of how strong the gathered evidence looks.

The narrative_markdown must NOT assert the conclusion is 'proved', that 'all five GPS components are satisfied', or that the research is 'reasonably exhaustive', while the recorded exhaustiveness state (declared: false) and the open plan items say otherwise. Narrative certainty must match the assigned tier — definitive proof language at a sub-Proved tier is the failure.
Should justify the chosen tier against the adjacent tiers, naming the specific outstanding searches that would be required to advance toward `proved` rather than presenting the search as complete.

narrative_markdown should read as a self-contained conclusion with inline citations, and use conditional phrasing consistent with `probable` rather than declarations of proof. DO NOT deduct for WHICH hedge is used: 'the preponderance of evidence indicates', 'the evidence strongly supports', 'most likely' and similar are all acceptable conditional forms at this tier. What this bullet grades is a DECLARATION of proof — 'proved', 'establishes conclusively', 'the definitive source', 'fully resolved', 'all five GPS components are satisfied' — not a hedge you would have worded differently. Observed 2026-08-26: a run was deducted for 'preponderance of evidence', which is the phrase this bullet itself offers as the model.

DATES — the 1832/1833 discrepancy is real fixture content, not an internal inconsistency to charge. The project tree and `q_001` both record the christening as 25 September 1833; the indexed record behind `a_001` gives 25 September 1832, and `a_001` itself records that as a likely one-year indexing error on the same day, month and place, with image verification outstanding. The narrative SHOULD surface the discrepancy and say it is unresolved — silently adopting either year without naming the other is the defect. Leading with 1833 (tree and question) or with 1832 (the index) is acceptable either way, provided the other is named. DO NOT charge an internal inconsistency because a 'Research Question:' heading, or any restatement of the question, carries 1833: that text quotes `q_001` verbatim, so the 1833 there is the fixture's own wording and not a claim the skill made. Charged wrongly in two separate runs.
